summary: The disappearance of General Chris McCasland, the Air Force's former UAP authority, has become the week's dominant story after investigative journalist Ross Coulthart reported security footage showing McCasland never leaving his home before vanishing, with law enforcement now investigating potential foul play. Meanwhile, a former Air Force officer came forward to detail UFO incidents at a Montana base during the Cold War, adding historical weight to longstanding accounts that the military has tracked UAP activity for decades. The week also surfaced claims that whistleblowers in this space have faced credible threats, underscoring why some who possess classified information remain reluctant to speak publicly. Internet sleuths spotted what appears to be a newly registered aliens.gov domain, sparking speculation about possible government communication plans, though no official announcement has followed. With the FY2026 NDAA UAP briefing deadline set for June 30 and the Contact in the Desert conference coming in May, pressure continues to mount on federal agencies to clarify what they know about these incidents.
